text: Newport Beach City Councilmember, District 3
Four years ago, you entrusted me with the honor of representing you on the Newport Beach City Council.
My top priority was ensuring our Police and Fire Departments had the resources needed to keep Newport Beach safe, while being a responsible steward of your tax dollars.
Over the past four years, that commitment has led to:
Crime at an all-time low. This year alone, crime is down 12.7%.
Decreased the number of people living on our streets from nearly 100 to just six.
Invested in public safety technology that has helped lead to hundreds of arrests and the recovery of millions of dollars in stolen property.
Added a third fully staffed paramedic unit, improving emergency response times throughout the city.
Fully staffed our first responders while maintaining budget surpluses and protecting the city’s top AAA credit rating.

These results are why I am proudly endorsed by Newport Beach Firefighters; Lifeguards; Police Officers; and Orange County Sheriff, Don Barnes. They know I will continue fighting to protect our community and preserve the values that make our city such a special place.
If re-elected, I will continue to work tirelessly for you and our city. I respectfully ask for your vote.
www.Erik4Newport.com

text: Author
My family moved to Newport Beach in 1972 and my parents were immediately involved in the community. Like them I am dedicated to preserving the great qualities of Newport Beach.
My priorities on the City Council would include:
Saving Civic Center Park: Stop the City Council from destroying a beloved city park to build a police station. I support a new police complex, but it must not be built on park land.

Improving Public Safety: Ensure that our citizens feel safe in their homes and on our streets at all times. We should have both an independent external investigation of the recent July Fourth rioting and looting. We should identify and implement citywide preventative strategies.
Supporting Fiscal Accountability: Ask the tough questions about proposed spending and rein in the recent rapid growth in city expenses.

I have extensive financial experience, including five years at the US Securities and Exchange Commission and four years as a senior lawyer for Fidelity Investments. I serve on the boards of the Pacific Symphony and the Library Foundation of Newport Beach.
I would be honored to serve Newport Beach on the City Council.

text: Retired Construction Executive
The question is not, what have I done in the past, the question is, what is my vision for Newport Beach.
I am Tim Stoaks and I love this town.
Relieve traffic congestion in CdM by eliminating the toll booth at Newport Coast Drive so that South County Commuters go around CdM and not through it;
Enhance the state mandate City’s General plans requirement for additional housing by annexation of the 114-Acre Santa Ana Country Club to the City of Newport Beach. Grow the city;
Constructing, through strong fiscal management, a multi-functional community center for West Newport;

Newport does not need a New Police Headquarters; it needs a substation concept for where the challenges are. Focusing on the Peninsula where we have consistent police and emergency services requirement;
Protecting our Civic Center sculpture garden to include all major parks in the city;
Fully fund and expand senior services programming like the Oasis Senior Center;
Listen to neighborhood organizations and local residents to best determine what the city can do for them in their neighborhoods.
Government is here to listen to the community and My job, after listening, is to make those needs and wants into realities.
Keeping Newport, Newport.
